issues.legal_issue: A tenant claiming a statutory right of pre-emption must retain the qualifying tenancy through the decree, and cannot succeed after the tenancy has ended and the tenant has been dispossessed.
material_facts: The claimant had been a tenant-at-will of the land under its former owner when the land was sold.
The purchasers obtained a decree for the claimant's eviction, and the claimant was dispossessed before filing the pre-emption suit.
The claimant's tenancy had ended before the pre-emption suit was instituted.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could not obtain possession by pre-emption because he no longer held the land as a tenant and had lost his qualifying status before the decree; the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under s. 15(1)(a) Fourthly of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913, the right vests in a tenant who holds the land under tenancy of the vendor. The settled rule is that a pre-emptor must retain the qualification to pre-empt through the decree. The Court relied on Hans Nath v. Ragho Prasad Singh, Thakur Madho Singh v. Lt. James R. R. Skinner, Faiz Mohammad v. Fajar Ali Khan, Surjit Singh v. Gurnam Singh, and Ramji Lal v. State of Punjab, which it approved; it overruled Kashmiri Lal v. Chuhar Ram and Sohan Singh v. Udho Ram. The statutory right attaches to the land, and a tenant whose tenancy has ended no longer meets the requirement of holding the land as a tenant.

rule.if: preemption_suit and claimant_tenant_at_sale and (tenancy_ended_before_suit or tenancy_ended_during_suit_before_decree)

predicates.preemption_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking possession by pre-emption.
predicates.claimant_tenant_at_sale: The claimant held the land as a tenant under the seller when the land was sold.
predicates.tenancy_ended_before_suit: The claimant's tenancy ended before the pre-emption suit was filed.
predicates.tenancy_ended_during_suit_before_decree: The claimant's tenancy ended while the pre-emption suit was pending and before the decree was made.
predicates.claimant_cannot_succeed_in_preemption: The claimant cannot obtain possession by pre-emption.

issues.definition: When a claimant who was a tenant at the sale brings a pre-emption suit but the tenancy ends before the suit or before its decree, the claimant cannot succeed.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot reopen on appeal a factual issue that was not raised in the courts below and would require further factual investigation.
material_facts: In the appeal, the claimant applied to reopen the question of which land was covered by the earlier eviction decree.
The question had not been raised in the courts below and would have required investigation into the facts.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to reopen the question at the appellate stage.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated an unraised factual question requiring investigation as unsuitable for reopening at this stage of the appeal; it cited no statute or earlier case for this procedural conclusion.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is before a court hearing an appeal.
predicates.new_factual_issue_not_raised_below: A party seeks to raise a factual issue that was not raised in the courts below.
predicates.issue_requires_factual_investigation: Deciding the issue would require investigation into facts.
predicates.court_declines_to_reopen_issue: The court declines to reopen the factual issue at the appellate stage.

issues.definition: In an appeal, when a party raises a new factual issue that requires investigation, the court declines to reopen it.
